His strongest current positioning is building and working with agents, agent skills, AI employee workflows, automation, memory systems, computer vision, explainable AI, and practical software systems.

title: Current AI direction
summary: Deepak's strongest current direction is Agentic AI Engineering: building agents, designing skills for them, exploring how AI employees can be trained to work for a person, automating agent workflows, and reducing waste through better memory and context routing.

summary: Deepak is targeting Agentic AI Engineer roles across agent infrastructure, applied AI automation, AI research engineering, developer tools, and product AI. He is especially interested in building agents, working with agent skills, training AI employees, automating workflows like Gmail or information updates, researching new AI tools, experimenting with models, and turning that research into useful AI products.

title: AI employee vision
summary: Deepak defines an AI employee as an AI system trained to work for him by finding information, adapting to his style, preparing useful outputs, and updating him on a schedule with review in the loop. His first planned workflows are a LinkedIn skill-based posting assistant and an Instagram content assistant for Deepak AI. Both start from research, turn examples into reusable skills, prepare schedule-ready content, and require Deepak's approval before publishing.

title: LinkedIn AI employee workflow
summary: Deepak wants a LinkedIn AI employee because he is a LinkedIn enthusiast and wants to post more consistently about AI. The workflow studies strong LinkedIn posts, organizes patterns in an Excel sheet, turns those examples into a reusable skill.md, and uses that skill with fresh AI news or internet research to draft and schedule posts in Deepak's style, with Deepak approving before anything is published.

title: Instagram AI employee workflow
summary: Deepak has started an Instagram page called Deepak AI and wants an AI employee that turns researched AI topics into visual content ideas, images, short videos, voice or audio assets, and post drafts. The workflow may use tools such as HeyGen, Suno, ElevenLabs, image generation, and writing assistants, with the AI employee coordinating production and scheduling while Deepak approves before publishing.

title: Agent skill definition
summary: Deepak thinks of an agent skill as a reusable capability an AI agent can learn from structured input and call again for a repeated task. For example, he might give an agent an Excel sheet of strong LinkedIn examples, ask it to build a skill.md, and then use that skill to draft future posts from fresh research.

title: ASMOS
summary: ASMOS, also described by Deepak as an Adaptive Semantic Memory Operating System, is his flagship multi-agent memory project. It is a research-grade working prototype, not just a paper idea: Deepak reports code for routing, scoring, and memory; 400+ passing tests; Docker support; and experiments on Stack Overflow Q&A data with real AI models. ASMOS uses verified checkpoints to identify topic owners and load only the relevant memory slice. The final re-test showed about 22% token reduction, with results roughly in the 18-26% range depending on the question.

title: ASMOS evaluation
summary: Deepak evaluated ASMOS by comparing the actual prompt text sent to AI models in two modes: a baseline that loads broad memory and an ASMOS mode that loads only the owner agent's relevant memory. Tokens were counted with a real tokenizer across 50 questions and 10 random-seed reruns, then checked for statistical significance. The final result is about 22% token reduction, with an observed range around 18-26%.

title: ASMOS ownership scoring
summary: ASMOS chooses a topic owner with a weighted score: 60% trust, based on how often an agent's past answers were verified correct, and 40% contribution share, based on what fraction of correct answers on that topic came from that agent. New agents begin with a modest default trust score so they are not locked out. If nobody stands out clearly enough, ASMOS falls back to broader memory search instead of forcing a close guess.

title: Deepak.ai
summary: Deepak.ai is Deepak's portfolio and personal AI surface. He sees it as his second strongest current project because it turns the portfolio into an agentic workflow: a public site, documented memory, and Dex as a constrained AI recall layer. To recruiters, it should prove that Deepak loves automation, building agents, experimenting with available AI models, and building AI products that remove repeated manual work.

title: Turb-DETR
summary: Turb-DETR is Deepak's turbidity-aware underwater plastic detection project. It adapts an RT-DETR-style transformer detector for murky underwater conditions, with turbidity-aware augmentation, reproducible evaluation, and a focus on real-time deployment realism.

title: ShortcutScore
summary: ShortcutScore is Deepak's explainable AI project for measuring shortcut learning severity in deep models. It focuses on making spurious correlations measurable instead of relying only on qualitative inspection.

title: Dental AI Pipeline
summary: The Dental AI Pipeline is Deepak's medical computer vision project for panoramic OPG X-rays. It decomposes the problem into tooth detection, cropping, disease-specific analysis for caries and periodontal bone loss, severity estimation, and structured reporting.

title: Docksmith Engine
summary: Docksmith Engine is Deepak's Go systems project for understanding container internals. It rebuilds core container-runtime ideas such as file layering, deterministic caching, Docksmithfile parsing, filesystem setup, and process isolation.

title: PESU Vault
summary: PESU Vault is Deepak's automation tool for downloading university course materials from PESU Academy. It uses FastAPI, Playwright, persistent browser-session handling, and organized downloads to solve a real student workflow.

title: SahayAI leadership

Regardless of automation level, AI employees are never allowed to touch Gmail or email content, saved passwords or payment info, or direct messages, and they can never auto-publish without Deepak's approval.
